companies.lead: Choose the project company for each role in the template. Folder permissions and approval steps are given to these companies. Permissions of a role left empty are skipped and its steps go to the project administrators. The code is the company code in the naming standard.

entry.lead: Set up the project step by step with the wizard, or create it quickly from a template and change the settings later.
entry.wizardHint: 11 steps: language, template, parties and task teams, people, folders, document codes, workflows and the ISO 19650 rules.
entry.quickHint: A template, a name and a code; everything else as the template sets it.

setup.restored: Your unfinished setup was restored from this browser.

leads.language: The language of the project's folder, workflow and list names. Each person's interface language stays their own.
leads.template: A template brings folders, permissions, naming standards, workflows and the ISO 19650 settings. Parts that belong to an Enterprise module are skipped when the module is not installed.
leads.basics: The project code is written into the document codes, so keep it short.
leads.parties: Map each party of the template to a company. Folder permissions and approval steps go to these companies; every party with a task team gets its own work-in-progress area. Choose the lead appointed party.
leads.people: Add people who already have a SiteKeep account. They join the company of their party, its task team and the project roles you choose.
leads.folders: The folder tree comes from the template. Add folders below the template's folders, or leave out folders that carry no ISO 19650 state.
leads.naming: The document code standard gives every document a unique code from work in progress on. Adjust the codes of the list fields and check a sample name.
leads.codes: Revision and suitability codes are kept per version. ISO 19650 uses P01 / C01 revisions; the legacy profile R00, R01 … as on many sites.
leads.workflows: The ISO 19650 transition table and the template's workflows. Choose who approves each step: a party's task team, a project role or the project administrators.
leads.rules: Enforcement makes the transition table binding from the start. A task team's work in progress can be closed to the other teams.
leads.summary: The server checks the whole setup before anything is created.
